source.title: ExpertPlex: A High-Goodput Disaggregated Serving System for MoE LLMs with Adaptive Persistent Kernels
source.summary: LLMs scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) parameters for superior intelligence, but massive weights and dynamic computation impede efficient serving. Existing instance-level prefill-decode disaggregation isolates the phases on separate full-model replicas. As MoE weights grow, each instance may span tens to hundreds of GPUs, making resource allocation increasingly coarse. Configured prefill-to-decode ratios thus often mismatch demand, overprovisioning one phase while overloading the other. Prefill-decode colocation avoids this duplication, but existing Green Context solutions partition each GPU by phase and fix phase resources during a kernel. They cannot track resource changes across operations or layerwise variation in routed expert load, causing head-of-line blocking or idle reserved resources. Partitioning every GPU also leaves each phase with fewer local resources, forces wider parallelism and more communication, and lets prefill and decode traffic interfere on the shared network. We present ExpertPlex, which shares massive MoE experts across phases while disaggregating lightweight attention modules. Expert sharing eliminates over 95% of duplicate model weights and multiplexes dynamically sparse computation, while attention disaggregation reduces attention communication cost. ExpertPlex further uses (1) adaptive persistent kernels to schedule dynamic expert computation at tile granularity for efficient, isolated execution; (2) attention-initiated MoE communication to avoid network interference and enable cross-phase communication-computation overlap; and (3) a tile-to-cluster model to optimize these mechanisms for maximum goodput. Experiments serving MiniMax-M2.7 and GLM-5.1-FP8 show that ExpertPlex improves goodput by up to 2.01$\times$ over instance-level prefill-decode disaggregation and 1.66$\times$ over prefill-decode colocation.

previous_facts.title: ExpertPlex: A High-Goodput Disaggregated Serving System for MoE LLMs with Adaptive Persistent Kernels
previous_facts.event_hint: New MoE LLM serving system (ExpertPlex) that shares experts across prefill/decode while disaggregating attention, with adaptive persistent kernels and attention-initiated MoE communication.
previous_facts.problem: Instance-level prefill-decode disaggregation (PDD) for MoE LLMs isolates phases on separate full-model replicas; as MoE weights grow each instance spans tens to hundreds of GPUs, so configured P:D ratios mismatch demand (overprovisioning one phase, overloading the other). Prefill-decode colocation avoids duplication, but Green Context-style spatial partitioning fixes per-kernel phase resources and cannot track resource changes across operations or layerwise variation in routed expert load, causing head-of-line blocking or idle reserved resource bubbles; partitioning every GPU also widens parallelism/communication and lets prefill+decode traffic interfere on the shared network.
previous_facts.mechanism: ExpertPlex shares massive MoE experts across phases while disaggregating lightweight attention modules to the MoE-attention boundary. Three mechanisms: (1) adaptive persistent kernels (APK) that schedule dynamic expert computation at tile granularity for efficient, isolated execution with tile-boundary preemption (no checkpoint/restore/recompute); (2) attention-initiated MoE communication to avoid cross-phase network interference and enable cross-phase communication-computation overlap; (3) a tile-to-cluster model to optimize the mechanisms for maximum goodput. Expert sharing eliminates over 95% of duplicate model weights and multiplexes dynamically sparse expert computation.

evidence.claim: Expert sharing eliminates over 95% of duplicate model weights by sharing MoE experts across prefill and decode phases.
evidence.condition: MoE experts shared across phases while attention is disaggregated; conceptual claim from abstract

evidence.claim: ExpertPlex improves goodput by up to 2.01x over instance-level prefill-decode disaggregation and up to 1.66x over prefill-decode colocation across MiniMax-M2.7 and GLM-5.1-FP8 workloads.
evidence.condition: Serving MiniMax-M2.7 and GLM-5.1-FP8 on NVIDIA H800 nodes; headline abstract claim, per-setting breakdown only spelled out for MiniMax-M2.7 ShareGPT in visible evidence

evidence.claim: On MiniMax-M2.7 / ShareGPT under the joint TTFT (1s) and TPOT (50ms) SLO, ExpertPlex reaches 11.3 requests/s/node P90 goodput: 2.01x over SGLang-PDD, 2.72x over SGLang-Colocated, 5.65x over SGLang-ChunkedPrefill, and 1.41x over SGLang-PDMux.
evidence.condition: MiniMax-M2.7, ShareGPT, P90 goodput (joint TTFT 1s + TPOT 50ms), H800

evidence.claim: Under tuned GEMM/data-processing tiles, all MiniMax-M2.7 MoE operations have preemption intervals below 25.3 us and GEMM intervals below 10.7 us; the interval depends on tile execution time not token count, allowing a short decode op to preempt a prefill request with thousands of input tokens. REEF's best reported delay is 35 us and requires recomputing the preempted kernel (reference points only).
evidence.baseline: REEF best 35 us (reference); LithOS 250 us, Bless 700 us, GPreempt 100 us (reference points, not MoE-targeted)
evidence.condition: MiniMax-M2.7, tuned tiles; comparison baselines do not target MoE workloads
evidence.source_locator: Section 7.6 Analysis of Preemption Intervals / Figure 15, PDF Page 12

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Hardware: single-node = one NVIDIA H800 node with 8 GPUs via NVLink; multi-node = up to 3 machines, each 8 H800 GPUs via NVLink, machines linked by 8x 200 Gbps InfiniBand NICs per node. Throughput reported as requests/s/node. Main metric: P90 goodput (highest arrival rate with >=90% of requests meeting both TTFT and TPOT SLOs). Models: MiniMax-M2.7 (1P1D under PDD) and GLM-5.1-FP8. Workloads: ShareGPT (short) and LooGLE (long), Poisson arrivals. SLOs per model/workload (e.g. MiniMax-M2.7 ShareGPT TTFT 1s/TPOT 50ms; LooGLE TTFT 10s/TPOT 100ms; GLM-5.1-FP8 ShareGPT TTFT 2s/TPOT 100ms). Baselines all SGLang-based: SGLang-Colocated, SGLang-ChunkedPrefill, SGLang-PDD, SGLang-PDMux (MuxWise/Green Context, modified for MoE).
previous_facts.limitations: GLM-5.1-FP8 runs out of memory under the 1P1D PDD layout on 24 GPUs, so GLM-5.1-FP8 PDD numbers are not reported. Several baselines cannot express ExpertPlex's 24-GPU fine-grained layout under their parallelism constraints; for GLM-5.1-FP8 those baselines run on the largest compatible 16-GPU layout and are compared via request rates per node. SGLang-PDMux is compatible only with tensor-parallel attention. Multi-node evaluation limited to up to 3 machines. Preemption-interval comparison baselines (LithOS, Bless, GPreempt, PipeSwitch, REEF) are reference points only since they do not target MoE LLM workloads and lack modern MoE kernel features (TMA multicast, CTA clusters, warp specialization, CUDA Graph). The headline abstract speedups are spelled out only for the MiniMax-M2.7/ShareGPT setting in the visible front evidence; per-setting multipliers for GLM-5.1-FP8 and LooGLE are not visible.
previous_facts.project_relevance: ExpertPlex disaggregates attention by phase while sharing MoE experts, and its attention-initiated MoE communication is a phase-aware network mechanism that isolates prefill vs decode traffic and enables cross-phase communication-computation overlap to avoid network interference. This is directly relevant to the TPN topic's questions about whether serving-network mechanisms can perceive the inference phase and KV-cache position and whether network-side traffic isolation reduces cross-phase interference. However, ExpertPlex's contribution sits at MoE-dispatch/attention disaggregation within an LLM serving cluster rather than being a general Token Performance Network, and the paper reports TTFT/TPOT-goodput and per-node throughput rather than isolated network-utilization or cross-node KV-cache-transfer metrics. (Project inference, separate from source facts.)
